assessments.reasoning: The three gcc-mirror/gcc captures cover consecutive byte ranges [0,16384), [16384,32768) and [32768,35295) at the same commit and path. Each reports the claim’s whole-file SHA-256, 71b8d73e46e0c31b1dc91ba5306f5ef0af009273b3bb283f31d8dad69666fa9e. Header lines 3–27 contain the attribution, timestamp, version choice and both exception sentences. The rest of the file supplies no conflicting notice.

Software Commons’ own docs/SCOPE.md at cdff8aeed68bf1f9c62d8c86159c7dc08b2d75d7 defines the exception criterion at bytes [640,783). It admits an additional permission with the affected editions supported separately. It assigns editorial crosswalks to the index and SPDX list membership to SPDX. Those boundaries fit the proposed mapping.

challenge.method: Applied SCES-1.0 §§2–4 and 7 at policy commit ab26f278422772f2d9e5d4dd016407d14372a710, with supplied adopted bundle SHA-256 14da3f31f697ab828d4a4560f060dbe511861020db54bea7bc531e20ea0855ce. These provisions require direct inspection, separate assessments of byte integrity and source authority, exact edition and scope, and a targeted challenge to an identity merge. Following protocol stage 7, I reopened the complete file and checked whether its latest-version reference or its comment about uniformity across GNU packages justified substituting another witness.
challenge.results: The Savannah URL identifies where to get the latest GNU Config config.sub. It supplies no immutable upstream revision or copy history. The comment that the file is “supposed to be the same” across GNU packages is a statement of intent. The decisive evidence is the notice in the pinned downstream file itself.

limitations: The timestamp is an in-file date. The first publication of the clause, the origin of these bytes and their identity with a particular GNU Config revision remain unestablished.
Applicability to any other file, package or release requires evidence for that object. The finding concerns the presence and wording of a conditional permission.
reasoning: The GNU Compiler Collection mirror publishes the inspected root-level config.sub at commit 04696df09633baf97cdbbdd6e9929b9d472161d3. Its header credits “Copyright 1992-2021 Free Software Foundation, Inc.” and sets timestamp='2021-10-27'. The inline exception permits inclusion of this file under the rest of a program’s distribution terms if the program contains a configuration script generated by Autoconf. The next sentence expressly designates that exception as additional permission under GPLv3 section 7. This meets the index’s admission criterion for an exception. The name and active state are the index’s editorial mapping.
